extracted.intended_audience: researchers, graduate students, and users of Macaulay2 interested in computational algebraic geometry and reproducing the book's examples
extracted.subtask_description: Information and resources for using the book 'Computations in algebraic geometry with Macaulay 2' — what the book provides (chapters, goals, prerequisites), where to get the source code, and available formats. Useful for readers who want to learn from, reproduce, or run the book's Macaulay2 examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Macaulay2 code availability (book)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Macaulay2 code used in the book is available in machine readable form at https://github.com/Macaulay2/M2/tree/master/M2/Macaulay2/tests/ComputationsBook, with one subdirectory per chapter. Each file */chapter.m2 contains the original code from the chapter, whereas the file */test.m2 contains code slightly updated to run properly with the latest version of Macaulay2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the chapter subdirectory to find original examples and the test.m2 files for updated code that runs on current Macaulay2; this supports reproducibility and adaptation of the book's computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Book formats and figures availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire book, except for the cover and the front matter, is available in dvi (with needed figures: octahedron.eps, standardpairs-fixed.eps, and Y25.eps), postscript, and pdf. Preface and each chapter are available in dvi, postscript, and pdf. The cover and the front matter are available separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When accessing or reproducing figures or examples, ensure you obtain the listed EPS files; use the per-chapter files (dvi/ps/pdf) for targeted reading or printing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisite knowledge (Gröbner bases)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the chapter 'Ideals, Varieties, and Macaulay2' familiarity with Gröbner bases is assumed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers without background in Gröbner bases should obtain introductory material before using that chapter's examples; the book is not introductory on that topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter learning objective — Ideals, Varieties, and Macaulay2
rubrics_metrics.description: This chapter introduces Macaulay2 commands for some elementary computations in algebraic geometry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to teach basic Macaulay2 usage for algebraic geometry computations through examples; assumes prior theoretical background (e.g., Gröbner bases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter learning objective — Projective Geometry and Homological Algebra
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an introduction to many of the homological commands in Macaulay2 (modules, free resolutions, Ext and Tor, ...), by means of examples showing how to use homological tools to study projective varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus is on practical use of homological commands via examples; readers should follow the examples to learn homological computations in Macaulay2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter learning objective — Data Types, Functions, and Programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Present an introduction to the structure of Macaulay2 commands and the writing of functions in the Macaulay2 language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this chapter to learn how to write and structure Macaulay2 code; consult the Macaulay2 manual for further details as suggested by the authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter learning objective — Teaching the Geometry of Schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Presents a collection of graduate level problems in algebraic geometry illustrating the power of Macaulay2 as an educational tool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed for graduate instruction; instructors can adopt problems and examples to teach scheme-theoretic computations with Macaulay2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter learning objective — Monomial Ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrates how to implement algorithms in Macaulay2 for studying and using monomial ideals, illustrating methods with examples from combinatorics, integer programming, and algebraic geometry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes algorithm implementation and applied examples; useful for readers interested in connections between combinatorics, optimization, and algebraic geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter learning objective — Enumerative Geometry to Solving Systems of Polynomial Equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Macaulay2 to investigate problems from enumerative geometry, illustrating applications of symbolic computation to solving systems of polynomial equations, including overdetermined, deficient, and improper systems, and addressing real solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for studying solution counting and computational techniques for polynomial systems; pay attention to sections on real solutions and special system types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter learning objective — Resolutions and Cohomology over Complete Intersections
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains a new proof and new applications of a theorem of Shamash and Eisenbud, providing a construction of projective resolutions of modules over a complete intersection and showing how to write Macaulay2 code to implement the construction and compute Ext modules simultaneously in all homological degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced chapter combining theoretical results with explicit Macaulay2 implementation; follow the provided code to reproduce invariants hard to obtain by hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter learning objective — Algorithms for the Toric Hilbert Scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrate the use of Macaulay2 for exploring the structure of toric Hilbert schemes, encountering algorithms from commutative algebra, algebraic geometry, polyhedral theory and geometric combinatorics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended for computational exploration of toric Hilbert schemes; readers should be prepared for interdisciplinary algorithmic content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter learning objective — Sheaf Algorithms Using the Exterior Algebra
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain constructive methods for computing the cohomology of a sheaf on a projective variety, give a construction for the Beilinson monad, and provide examples illustrating the use of the Beilinson monad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the chapter to learn constructive cohomology computations and the Beilinson monad implementation in Macaulay2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter learning objective — Needles in a Haystack: Special Varieties via Small Fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrate how picking points over a finite field at random can help investigate algebraic geometry questions; develop a program that produces random curves of genus g < 15, test Green's Conjecture on syzygies of canonical curves, and produce Calabi–Yau 3-folds of degree 17 in P^6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows stochastic/computational experimentation techniques; useful for empirical investigations and conjecture testing using Macaulay2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter learning objective — D-modules and Cohomology of Varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce ideas from differential operators and show how to use these concepts in conjunction with Macaulay2 to obtain new information about polynomials and their algebraic varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bridges D-module theory and computational practice; follow examples to apply differential-operator techniques in Macaulay2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on examples, implementations, and reproducibility across chapters
rubrics_metrics.description: Many chapters provide code, constructive methods, and examples showing how to implement theoretical constructions in Macaulay2 (e.g., implementing algorithms, writing code for constructions, using the computer to determine invariants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect the book to be hands-on: to learn from it, run and adapt the provided chapter.m2/test.m2 files and follow examples to reproduce results and experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource pointers and further documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The page links to the Macaulay2 manual distributed with the program, Macaulay2 documentation, community resources (discussion group, Zulip), packages, source code on GitHub, and instructions on installation and changes by version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the listed resources for installation help, deeper language documentation, package development, and community support; consult the manual for language details referenced by chapters.
